title: Caterpillar Q2 2026 — Construction Industries Executive Brief

statements.text: Disclosed Construction Industries dealer inventory increased $1.5 billion in Q1 2026 and $400 million in Q2 2026.
Reported CI sales growth was 34.8% in Q2 2026, compared with 38.1% in Q1 2026.
Caterpillar's Q2 2026 release said higher sales volume was mainly driven by higher sales of equipment to end users and by the impact from changes in dealer inventories.

We read the change between Q1 and Q2 2026 as consistent with a shift in the composition of growth toward end-user demand: the disclosed CI dealer build fell from $1.5 billion to $400 million while World retail growth rose from 7% to 22%.

Retail growth is reported in price-neutral dollars and only to the whole percent, while reported sales and dealer-inventory dollars are current-price; these figures support a directional reading and do not form an additive bridge.
Reading the order in which management lists volume drivers as a ranking by size is an unsourced assumption, not a disclosed fact, and that evidence still needs review.
Q2 2026 CI segment profit rose $703M year over year.

No Q2 2026 CI segment profit driver is quantified in the benchmark, so the $703M increase remains entirely unassigned and the profit bridge is unresolved; the prior-year profit comparative has also not been tested for restatement.
The Q1 2026 and prior-year CI segment profit bridges are also unresolved, with residuals of $12M and $14M left unassigned to any itemized driver.
